description:
Banner is a prominent message used to promote a feature, offer, event, or announcement. Its purpose is to market or inform proactively, not to respond to something the user did. To communicate system or account status (errors, warnings, confirmations), use [Alert](Alert) instead. Place a page-level Banner at the top of the main content area, above or just below the H1. Use one Banner per region at a time. Stacked banners get ignored or can create competing hierarchy and message fatigue. ```js --- type: example --- Enroll in summer courses before June 1 to secure your spot. Places are limited and usually fill up within weeks. ``` ### Variant Use `relaxed` (default) for standalone banners and `compact` where space is tight. `compact` has smaller spacing, icon box and text. The `color` prop sets the background of the Banner and its icon box: `violet` (default) or `sea`. ```js --- type: example ---
Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.
``` ### Buttons in a Banner A Banner can contain buttons to let the user act on the message. Use `primary` buttons, a filled one for the main action and one without background for the other. ```js --- type: example --- Your school now offers a free study skills course. Enroll by the end of the month to get access to all lessons. ``` ### Dismissing Setting `closeButtonLabel` renders a close button, which also makes the `Escape` key close the Banner while focus is inside it. The `timeout` prop dismisses the Banner automatically. `onDismiss` is called after the Banner closes. ```js --- type: example --- const Example = () => { const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(true) return (
{isOpen && ( setIsOpen(false)} > I fade out after 5 seconds. )}
) } render() ``` ### Screen reader announcement Given a `liveRegion`, the Banner sets `aria-live="polite"` on it and renders its title and content there, so screen readers announce a Banner that appears while the user is on the page. Use `isLiveRegionAtomic` to set `aria-atomic`. The live region element should be static, either server rendered or included in the static HTML of the app, because some screen readers ignore live regions added later. ```js --- type: example --- const Example = () => { const [banners, setBanners] = useState([]) const [count, setCount] = useState(0) const addBanner = () => { setBanners([...banners, count]) setCount(count + 1) } const closeBanner = (key) => setBanners(banners.filter((banner) => banner !== key)) return (
{banners.map((banner) => ( closeBanner(banner)} liveRegion={() => document.getElementById('flash-messages')} margin="general.spaceMd 0 0" > This banner is announced by screen readers. ))}
) } render() ``` ### Guidelines ```js --- type: embed --- ``` ```js --- type: embed --- ```

children.description: Content to be rendered within the Banner.

title.description: The first row of the Banner, displayed above the content.

color.description: The background color of the Banner and its icon box.

variant.description: `relaxed` has larger spacing and icon box, `compact` fits tight spaces.

renderIcon.description: An icon, or function that returns an icon, displayed in a colored box at the start of the Banner.

liveRegion.description: A DOM element or function that returns an element where the screen reader announcement is placed.

isLiveRegionAtomic.description: Value for the `aria-atomic` attribute of the live region, it controls whether the whole region or only the change is read.

timeout.description: Milliseconds until the Banner is dismissed automatically.

margin.description: Valid values are `0`, `none`, `auto`, and Spacing token values (see https://instructure.design/layout-spacing), applied with CSS-like shorthand, e.g. `margin="general.spaceMd auto"`.

closeButtonLabel.description: Screen reader label of the close button, setting it renders the close button.

onDismiss.description: Callback after the Banner is closed.

transition.description: Transition used to make the Banner appear and disappear.

open.description: Setting it from `true` to `false` closes the Banner from the outside and still runs the transition.

elementRef.description: Provides a reference to the underlying html root element.
